labelling_protocol: Every question was written by reading the cited documentation section at the corpus commit. relevant_sources use source#anchor keys that exist in data/processed/chunks.jsonl (checked by `python -m docqa check-questions`). answer_keywords list one group per required fact; any alternative in a group counts. Insufficient-evidence questions were checked with grep to confirm the topic is absent from the corpus. Splits were fixed before any tuning; the test split was never used to choose settings.

questions.question: How do I make a query parameter optional?
expected_answer_points: Give the parameter a default value of None
questions.notes: Section: 'declare optional query parameters, by setting their default to None'.

questions.question: If I declare a bool query parameter called short, what does FastAPI do when the client sends ?short=yes?
expected_answer_points: The value is converted to True
1, true, on, yes and case variations are all True
questions.notes: Section lists 1/True/true/on/yes as True, and 0/false/off/no as False.

questions.question: Why must the path operation for /users/me be declared before /users/{user_id}?
expected_answer_points: Path operations are evaluated in order
Otherwise /users/{user_id} would match /users/me with user_id = 'me'

questions.question: How can I restrict a path parameter to a fixed set of allowed values?
expected_answer_points: Use a standard Python Enum as the parameter type
questions.notes: Section 'Predefined values': use a standard Python Enum.

questions.question: How can I validate a query parameter against a regular expression?
expected_answer_points: Pass a pattern to Query
questions.notes: Section 'Add regular expressions': define a regular expression pattern.

questions.question: How do I enable CORS in a FastAPI application?
expected_answer_points: Import CORSMiddleware and add it with app.add_middleware
Provide the list of allowed origins (allow_origins)

questions.question: How do I start a FastAPI app with several worker processes?
expected_answer_points: Use the --workers command line option with fastapi run or uvicorn

questions.question: What is the lifespan parameter of the FastAPI app used for?
expected_answer_points: Defining startup and shutdown logic
An async context manager with yield: code before yield runs before requests are served, code after yield runs at shutdown

questions.question: How does FastAPI decide whether a function parameter is read from the path, the query string, or the request body?
expected_answer_points: Declared in the path -> path parameter
Singular type (int, str, ...) -> query parameter
Pydantic model -> request body
questions.notes: Section 'Request body + path + query parameters' lists the three rules.

questions.question: How do I make FastAPI expect a single body parameter nested under a JSON key instead of the model fields at the top level?
expected_answer_points: Use Body(embed=True)

questions.question: How can I omit fields that were not explicitly set from the response?
expected_answer_points: Set response_model_exclude_unset=True on the path operation decorator

questions.question: What HTTP status code does RedirectResponse use by default?
expected_answer_points: 307 Temporary Redirect
questions.notes: Section 'RedirectResponse': uses a 307 status code by default.

questions.question: How do I override a dependency while testing?
expected_answer_points: Use the app.dependency_overrides dict: key = original dependency, value = override
Reset by setting it to an empty dict

questions.question: How can I apply a dependency to every path operation in the whole application?
expected_answer_points: Pass dependencies to the FastAPI application instance

questions.question: My app runs behind a proxy that strips a path prefix. How do I tell FastAPI about the prefix?
expected_answer_points: Use the --root-path command line option (sets the ASGI root_path)

questions.question: Which form of the Docker CMD instruction should I use for a FastAPI container, and why?
expected_answer_points: The exec form
So FastAPI can shut down gracefully and lifespan events are triggered

questions.question: What does TrustedHostMiddleware do, and what response is sent when a request's Host header is not allowed?
expected_answer_points: Enforces a correctly set Host header to guard against HTTP Host Header attacks
Invalid requests get a 400 response

questions.question: Why does the HTTP Basic Auth example compare credentials with secrets.compare_digest instead of ==?
expected_answer_points: To protect against timing attacks: the comparison takes the same time regardless of where strings differ
questions.notes: Sections 'Timing Attacks' and 'Fix it with secrets.compare_digest()'.

questions.question: What is the difference between fastapi dev and fastapi run?
expected_answer_points: dev: development mode, auto-reload enabled, listens on 127.0.0.1
run: production mode, auto-reload disabled, listens on 0.0.0.0

questions.question: Which package must I install before using TestClient?
expected_answer_points: httpx

questions.question: How do I add per-client rate limiting to a FastAPI application?
expected_answer_points: The documentation does not cover rate limiting; the system should abstain
questions.notes: grep for 'rate limit', 'rate-limit', 'throttl' finds no file in the corpus.

questions.question: How do I send error reports from FastAPI to Sentry?
expected_answer_points: Sentry is not mentioned in the documentation; the system should abstain
questions.notes: grep for 'sentry' finds no file in the corpus.

questions.question: How do I make a query parameter required?
expected_answer_points: Do not declare a default value for it

questions.question: How do I declare a path parameter that itself contains a path with slashes, such as a file path?
expected_answer_points: Use the :path convertor from Starlette, e.g. /files/{file_path:path}

questions.question: The client sends a query parameter named item-query, which is not a valid Python name. How do I read it?
expected_answer_points: Declare an alias in Query, e.g. alias="item-query"

questions.question: How can one query parameter receive several values, like ?q=foo&q=bar?
expected_answer_points: Declare the parameter with a list type
You must use Query explicitly, otherwise it would be interpreted as a request body

questions.question: How do I mark a query parameter as deprecated in the API docs without removing it?
expected_answer_points: Pass deprecated=True to Query

questions.question: How do I pin the FastAPI version in a requirements.txt file?
expected_answer_points: Specify an exact version with ==, or a range such as >=0.112.0,<0.113.0

questions.question: How do I require a path parameter item_id to be an integer greater than or equal to 1?
expected_answer_points: Use Path with ge=1
questions.notes: Section 'Number validations: greater than or equal'.

questions.question: I added a singular parameter importance next to two body models and FastAPI reads it from the query string. How do I make it part of the JSON body?
expected_answer_points: Singular values are assumed to be query parameters
Declare it with Body to make it a body key

questions.question: If a path operation has both a return type annotation and a response_model, which one does FastAPI use?
expected_answer_points: response_model takes priority

questions.question: How do I disable response model generation but keep the return type annotation for type checkers?
expected_answer_points: Set response_model=None on the path operation

questions.question: How can I customize the response that is returned when request validation fails?
expected_answer_points: Register an exception handler for RequestValidationError with @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
The handler receives the Request and the exception

questions.question: What is the downside of allowing all origins with the "*" wildcard in CORSMiddleware?
expected_answer_points: It excludes anything involving credentials such as cookies and Authorization headers

questions.question: What arguments does BackgroundTasks.add_task() take?
expected_answer_points: A task function
Positional arguments passed to it in order
Keyword arguments passed to it

questions.question: What is the difference between mounting a sub-application and including an APIRouter?
expected_answer_points: A mounted application is completely independent
The main app's OpenAPI schema and docs do not include anything from the mounted application

questions.question: How do I write a custom HTTP middleware in FastAPI?
expected_answer_points: Decorate a function with @app.middleware("http")
It receives the request and call_next, and can modify the response

questions.question: Which attributes does an UploadFile object expose?
expected_answer_points: filename
content_type
file (a SpooledTemporaryFile)

questions.question: Why can I declare a header parameter as user_agent in Python and still receive the User-Agent header?
expected_answer_points: Header converts underscores to hyphens automatically
HTTP headers are case-insensitive
Disable with convert_underscores=False

questions.question: If I pass a lifespan parameter to FastAPI, what happens to startup and shutdown event handlers?
expected_answer_points: They are no longer called: it is all lifespan or all events, not both

questions.question: How do I set a default response class for all path operations of an app?
expected_answer_points: Use the default_response_class parameter when creating FastAPI or APIRouter

questions.question: Can I put a Pydantic model directly into a JSONResponse, and if not, what should I use?
expected_answer_points: No: convert it first with jsonable_encoder
questions.notes: Section 'Using the jsonable_encoder in a Response'.

questions.question: How do I enable GZip compression of responses and what parameters does the middleware accept?
expected_answer_points: Add GZipMiddleware
minimum_size (default 500 bytes)
compresslevel (1-9, default 9)

questions.question: How do I hide a path operation from the generated OpenAPI schema?
expected_answer_points: Set include_in_schema=False

questions.question: How do I serve Swagger UI at a different URL and disable ReDoc?
expected_answer_points: Set docs_url to the new path
Set redoc_url=None

questions.question: Since FastAPI 0.122.0, which status code do the built-in security utilities return after a failed authentication, and what did they return before?
expected_answer_points: 401 Unauthorized now (with a WWW-Authenticate header)
403 Forbidden before 0.122.0
questions.notes: Page 'Use old 403 authentication error status codes'.

questions.question: How can I turn off the OpenAPI schema and docs UIs in production using an environment variable?
expected_answer_points: Read openapi_url from Pydantic settings and pass it to FastAPI
Set the OPENAPI_URL environment variable to an empty string; /docs then returns 404
questions.notes: Section 'Conditional OpenAPI from settings and env vars'.

questions.question: When should I write a path operation function with async def instead of plain def?
expected_answer_points: Use async def when you call libraries with await
Use def when the library does not support await (most database libraries)
If unsure, use def

questions.question: Which ASGI servers does the deployment documentation list for running FastAPI?
expected_answer_points: Uvicorn (the default in the fastapi command)
Hypercorn, Daphne, Granian

questions.question: How long are Let's Encrypt certificates valid?
expected_answer_points: About 3 months
questions.notes: Sections 'Let's Encrypt' and 'Certificate Renewal': short-lived, about 3 months.

questions.question: How do I include an existing Flask (WSGI) app inside a FastAPI app?
expected_answer_points: Wrap it with WSGIMiddleware from a2wsgi and mount it under a path
fastapi.middleware.wsgi is deprecated

questions.question: If several dependencies share the same sub-dependency, how many times is it called per request, and how can I change that?
expected_answer_points: Only once per request; the value is cached
Set use_cache=False in Depends to call it every time
questions.notes: Section 'Using the same dependency multiple times'.

questions.question: How do I apply a partial update with PATCH so that fields the client did not send keep their stored values?
expected_answer_points: Use item.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) to get only the fields that were sent

questions.question: What is the default maximum request body size that FastAPI accepts?
expected_answer_points: Not documented in the corpus; the system should abstain
questions.notes: grep for 'body size' and 'max_body' finds nothing.

questions.question: Does FastAPI support HTTP/3, and how do I enable it?
expected_answer_points: HTTP/3 is not mentioned; the system should abstain
questions.notes: grep for 'HTTP/3' finds nothing (only HTTP/2 for Hypercorn).

questions.question: How do I export FastAPI request metrics to Prometheus?
expected_answer_points: Prometheus is not mentioned; the system should abstain

questions.question: How do I expose a gRPC service from a FastAPI application?
expected_answer_points: gRPC is not mentioned; the system should abstain

questions.question: How do I cache responses in memcached with FastAPI?
expected_answer_points: memcached is not mentioned; the system should abstain
